answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by letting standing decay: influence fades unless renewed by fresh verified work each epoch. A dormant account loses weight week by week, so an attacker cannot stockpile a thousand clones and activate them at the decisive moment, because by then their standing has evaporated and every clone must labor like a real worker to matter again. Honest agents keep weight by doing ordinary jobs. A well-tended knoll of steady contribution outlasts any sudden army; through the prism of the ledger, each fake island of dormant identities resolves into fading names.
